text.p: English premier league games on Thursday (kickoff times 1500 GMT unless stated, league positions in brackets):
Aston Villa (4) v Chelsea (8)

Villa on a high after Sunday's 5-0 demolition of Wimbledon as they aim for sixth successive win. Their home record excellent and the Villa Park defence the meanest in the league, conceding five goals in nine games.
Chelsea, who beat West Ham 3-1 on Saturday, are still likely to be without Gianluca Vialli, who has a hamstring injury, while player-coach Ruud Gullit may continue at centre-back.
Blackburn Rovers (19) v Newcastle United (6)

Struggling Blackburn, whose game against Middlesbrough was postponed last weekend, desperately need points but will have the incentive of playing against Alan Shearer, their 15 million pounds ($23.3 million) export to Tyneside.

Newcastle, whose 1-1 draw with Liverpool on Monday means they have now gone six games without a win, should welcome back David Batty, another ex-Blackburn player, from suspension. Steve Howey, David Ginola (both calf) and Faustino Asprilla (hamstring) doubtful.
Leeds (12) v Coventry (17)

Five successive clean sheets suggest that the Leeds defence is as tight as they come. But scoring goals remains a problem and manager George Graham may replace Ian Rush and Brian Deane with fit-again Tony Yeboah and Rodney Wallace.

Former Leeds man Gordon Strachan, now manager of Coventry, will want to continue the momentum built up by successive wins over Newcastle and Leicester. Key to his plans is goalkeeper Steve Ogrizovic who will break George Curtis' 26-year-old record of 543 matches for the club.
Liverpool (1) v Leicester (13)

Liverpool's 1-1 draw with Newcastle put them three points clear of Arsenal at the head of the league and manager Roy Evans looks set to name an unchanged side despite a slight ankle injury to Robbie Fowler who now has 19 goals this season.
Leicester determined to recover from a 2-0 weekend loss against Coventry but still have injury doubts over defenders Steve Walsh and Mike Whitlow.
Middlesbrough (18) v Everton (7)

After postponing last weekend's game against Blackburn because of an outbreak of influenza, Middlesborough are still so uncertain of their line-up that manager Bryan Robson and assistant Viv Anderson, both 40, could play. At least the wayward Brazilian, Emerson, looks a sure starter.

Everton hope to extend their unbeaten run to 13 league games. Midfielder John Ebbrell out until the New Year with a hairline fracture of the foot although Tony Grant has recovered from an ankle injury.
Nottingham Forest (20) v Manchester United (5)
After an unexpected win over Arsenal, Forest will need more inspiration from caretaker-coach Stuart Pearce and Nigel Clough if they are to climb off the bottom.

Their chances look slim if Manchester United produce the kind of display which destroyed Sunderland 5-0. Roy Keane and Gary Pallister both doubtful while England midfielder David Beckham may substitute again.
Sheffield Wednesday (9) v Arsenal (2) (1745 GMT)

Wednesday looking to maintain a good run which has produced a win over Liverpool and draws with Manchester United and Spurs. Graham Hyde likely to be missing in midfield again and Dutchman Orlando Trustfull takes his place.

Arsenal coach Arsene Wenger may simply hope his team can end the game with 11 men having had a man sent off in each of the last three outings. The country's top goalscorer, Ian Wright, was the latest to go, in Saturday's 2-1 defeat at Nottingham Forest.
Sunderland (14) v Derby (11)
After a 5-0 mauling by Manchester United, Sunderland need a quick recovery. Striker Martin Smith has a back injury which could mean a recall for Paul Stewart.

Derby, runners-up to Sunderland in last season's first division, will also be looking to bounce back after a 3-1 defeat by Southampton. Injuries have made defender Paul McGrath and striker Dean Sturridge doubtful
Tottenham (10) v Southampton (16)
With Chris Armstrong and Darren Anderton injured, Spurs are still struggling to find any consistency although the likely presence of new signing John Scales should give them more focus in defence.

Southampton, whose 3-1 win over Derby was their first in five games, still without Matt le Tissier in midfield but Dutch defender Ullrich van Gobbel returns from suspension and could replace Francis Benali.
Wimbledon (3) v West Ham (15)

After a 19-match unbeaten run, Wimbledon came down to earth on Sunday with a the drubbing at Aston Villa. Manager Joe Kinnear is likely to resist too many changes although Dean Holdsworth could return to the attack.

Defeat by Stockport County in the League Cup seemed to distract West Ham minds last weekend as they were outclassed by Chelsea. Their problems lie in attack where on-loan Mike Newell may again keep Romanian international Florin Raduciouiu on the bench.
